title: Repurposing Video Diffusion Transformers for Cross-View Temporal Object Correspondence
summary: Cross-view object correspondence identifies the same object across views. However, existing methods often rely on frame-wise matching or sequential tracking, which can propagate correspondence errors under appearance changes or occlusions. Therefore, we introduce cross-view temporal object correspondence, which requires preserving object identity across both views and time from a query mask. To address this, we propose XTrack, a unified framework which repurposes a pretrained video DiT with semantic and spatiotemporal priors for RGB-to-mask latent transport, jointly modeling cross-view matching and temporal tracking. However, naive video DiTs do not guarantee accurate cross-view grounding and often attend to semantically similar yet incorrect objects across views. Thus, we introduce focal cross-view attention alignment, hard negative conditioning, and local context crop strategies to ensure reliable grounding. Finally, beyond these architectural enhancements, we also tackle the lack of dense annotation by introducing a pseudo-label curation pipeline that converts sparse Ego-Exo4D annotations into dense supervision to enable effective video-level training. Our results demonstrate the effectiveness of XTrack as a unified framework, ensuring robust temporal consistency and identity preservation.

title: Honeycomb-Surfels: Compact Hexagonal Primitives for Efficient Scene Rendering and Reconstruction
summary: Novel view synthesis and 3D reconstruction have advanced rapidly with radiance fields and splatting, yet their memory and computational demands limit their use in resource-constrained settings. We introduce Hexels: novel planar hexagonal surface elements with a first-order spatial color field for efficient 3D scene and 2D image representation. Hexels exploit locally planar regions with smoothly varying appearance using fewer, larger primitives. Their hexagonal support provides an area- and boundary-efficient domain, while the local color field captures appearance variation within each primitive. Across 34 scenes, Hexels improve PSNR over memory-matched 2DGS by 4.53-7.38 dB across datasets while requiring lower training VRAM. We further ablate Hexels by showing that per primitive, Hexels outperform 2DGS by upto 4.74 dB while using lower training VRAM and having 2.31 times faster FPS. Even in unconstrained settings, Hexels offers complementary quality-memory trade-offs. For efficient 3D surface reconstruction, Hexels reduce error by 28.9% compared with memory-matched 2DGS across 15 DTU scans. On 6 Tanks and Temples surface scenes, Hexels achieves the highest mean F1 among compared methods (34.38%, versus 31.72% for 2DGS). We further also show that Hexels, as a general primitive, improves 2D image representation over Image-GS. Hexels push the Pareto frontier on the quality-efficiency trade-off of surface-aligned primitives.

title: Can Discrete Tokens Serve as Semantically Lossless Representations of Visual Signals?
summary: Discrete visual tokens represent vision in a discrete form analogous to language, offering a native interface for multimodal modeling under a shared next-token prediction objective. However, quantization error is widely assumed to cause unavoidable semantic loss, fundamentally limiting the semantic fidelity of discrete visual tokens and positioning continuous visual representations as an intrinsic upper bound. Using multimodal understanding as a proxy for semantic fidelity, we revisit this assumption and find quantization error unreliable, as discrete representations with substantially larger errors can achieve better understanding. Instead, the effective bit budget of discrete indices emerges as a key determinant of downstream performance. However, existing quantizers eventually saturate as additional codebooks contribute progressively less semantic information. As one approach to alleviating this saturation, we introduce Factorized Vector Quantization, which quantizes complementary, fixed-dimensional views of the visual feature with symmetric parallel codebooks. It continues to improve at larger bit budgets, ultimately matching continuous visual representations in multimodal understanding. Trained on industrial-scale multimodal data, our model achieves state-of-the-art performance among discrete-representation models, outperforming UniAR and Emu3-Chat by 22.8% and 59.2%, respectively, on a nine-metric average. To our knowledge, it is also the first discrete-representation model competitive with strong continuous-representation models such as Qwen3-VL, including on fine-grained OCR tasks. We further identify the key principles and a practical recipe enabling this competitiveness. These results and insights support the potential of discrete visual representations to underpin large-scale native multimodal foundation models. Code and models are available at https://github.com/hustvl/FVQ

title: Honeycomb-Surfels: Compact Hexagonal Primitives for Efficient Scene Rendering and Reconstruction
summary: Novel view synthesis and 3D reconstruction have advanced rapidly with radiance fields and splatting, yet their memory and computational demands limit their use in resource-constrained settings. We introduce Hexels: novel planar hexagonal surface elements with a first-order spatial color field for efficient 3D scene and 2D image representation. Hexels exploit locally planar regions with smoothly varying appearance using fewer, larger primitives. Their hexagonal support provides an area- and boundary-efficient domain, while the local color field captures appearance variation within each primitive. Across 34 scenes, Hexels improve PSNR over memory-matched 2DGS by 4.53-7.38 dB across datasets while requiring lower training VRAM. We further ablate Hexels by showing that per primitive, Hexels outperform 2DGS by upto 4.74 dB while using lower training VRAM and having 2.31 times faster FPS. Even in unconstrained settings, Hexels offers complementary quality-memory trade-offs. For efficient 3D surface reconstruction, Hexels reduce error by 28.9% compared with memory-matched 2DGS across 15 DTU scans. On 6 Tanks and Temples surface scenes, Hexels achieves the highest mean F1 among compared methods (34.38%, versus 31.72% for 2DGS). We further also show that Hexels, as a general primitive, improves 2D image representation over Image-GS. Hexels push the Pareto frontier on the quality-efficiency trade-off of surface-aligned primitives.

title: The Trinity:Capability-Driven Recursive Self-Improvement for Multimodal Agents
summary: Multimodal intelligence can be viewed as human-guided co-evolution between worlds and agents through interaction. However, scaling this process faces two bottlenecks: constructing heterogeneous, verifiable environments is costly, and manual Harness iteration cannot keep pace with growing task diversity and complexity. A key insight is that tasks with different modalities and surface forms can share the same underlying capability requirements. We therefore introduce The Trinity, a recursive self-improvement framework coupling world generation with Harness evolution through three roles: Creator, Explorer, and Evolver. Drawing on verified execution trajectories, Evolver shifts the basis of task organization from surface categories to shared requirements, reorganizing the original task tree into a hierarchical capability tree. We introduce Capability-Driven Real2Sim2Real: for heterogeneous tasks at the same node, Creator abstracts their common requirements into simplified, verifiable simulated worlds for capability learning, while evaluation on original tasks measures transfer. Along this capability tree, Explorer progressively evolves reusable capability modules through selective inheritance, forming a Harness tree whose validated updates accumulate across iterations within a fixed topology. The resulting Harnesses specialize in different capabilities, motivating a Capability-Aware Harness Router that uses public task information to select compatible module configurations from the tree. Our evolved Harnesses improve mean performance by 34 points across 28 training benchmarks and 26 points across 18 unseen benchmarks, including two real-world embodied tasks.

title: A Heart Means Recursion: Exploring Visual Meaning and Communication in VLMs
summary: Do vision-language models (VLMs) share our ability to communicate visually? We share preliminary findings, starting from a surprising observation: simple visual symbols like a red heart can strongly influence model behavior on seemingly unrelated tasks, such as steering models towards recursive solutions on simple coding problems. Notably, this steering effect is largely implicit, as models' direct interpretations and thinking traces about visual symbols diverge substantially from their observed behavior. In visual communication between models, this leads to a generation--interpretation gap: while models tend to send shape primitives that they (and humans) find intuitive, these visual cues often fail to steer other models. In further communication games involving abstract concepts and stories, models can creatively use visuals to transmit meaning to one another, although some communications remain non-intuitive to humans. These findings reveal that VLMs might be capable of rich, creative, and visually-grounded communication, but their interpretation and production of visual meaning diverges from human conventions in surprising ways. Together this work highlights both the promise and challenges of visual communication between humans and VLMs.

title: Learning Where to Trust: Reliability-Guided Expert Routing and Velocity Gating for 3D Deformable Registration
summary: Deformable image registration relies on accurate anatomical correspondences. However, explicitly coupling local matching reliability with spatial context selection and deformation update strength remains insufficiently explored in learning-based registration. This challenge is particularly pronounced in homogeneous, weakly textured, and severely deformed regions, where ambiguous matches may induce erroneous deformation updates. We propose ReliMorph, a reliability-routed symmetric framework for 3D deformable registration that couples correspondence assessment with spatial context selection and update strength.Local correlation distributions characterize correspondence ambiguity using shared anatomical features with modality-specific adaptation. These reliability cues guide spatial expert fusion and gate residual velocities during coarse-to-fine refinement. Updated inverse-inconsistency feedback guides routing and gating at finer pyramid levels. To our knowledge, ReliMorph is the first 3D deformable registration framework to jointly condition spatial expert routing and residual velocity gating on correspondence reliability. Extensive experiments demonstrate that ReliMorph consistently outperforms competing methods in anatomical overlap, highlighting its effectiveness across unimodal and multimodal registration tasks.

title: GUI-JEPA: Candidate-Conditioned JEPA Latents as a Fast Action Policy for Mobile GUI Agents
summary: Mobile GUI agents are typically fine-tuned 7B-scale vision-language models (VLMs) that generate each action as text. However, these VLMs decode every action token by token, and even agents that score candidate actions keep a large language model or VLM in the loop, making them slow and memory-hungry. To address these issues, we propose GUI-JEPA, to our knowledge the first decoder-free GUI agent policy built on a Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture (JEPA), which selects actions in the latent space of a JEPA encoder pretrained on unlabelled GUI screenshots. Its action- and region-conditioned latent predictor turns the screen latent into one latent per candidate action, letting lightweight heads score all candidates against the instruction in a single batched pass, without decoding a token. We further show that the scorer relies on this latent pathway and that the predictor is trained for the decision itself: a randomly initialised predictor does just as well as one pretrained on screen dynamics. On AndroidControl, GUI-JEPA is 2.8-4.0x faster on the same GPU than a Qwen2.5-VL-7B agent we fine-tune with the same inputs, while reaching 86-92% of its in-distribution accuracy with 6% of its parameters. Code is available at https://github.com/bcwang-sjtu/GUI-JEPA

title: TSE-Net: Semi-supervised monocular height estimation from single remote sensing images
summary: Monocular height estimation plays a critical role in 3D perception for remote sensing, offering a cost-effective alternative to multi-view or LiDAR-based methods. While deep learning has significantly advanced the capabilities of monocular height estimation, these methods remain fundamentally limited by the availability of labeled data, which are expensive and labor-intensive to obtain at scale. The scarcity of high-quality annotations hinders the generalization and performance of existing models. To overcome this limitation, we propose leveraging large volumes of unlabeled data through a semi-supervised learning framework, enabling the model to extract informative cues from unlabeled samples and improve its predictive performance. In this work, we introduce Teacher-Student-Exam Network (TSE-Net), a self-training pipeline for semi-supervised monocular height estimation. The pipeline integrates teacher, student, and exam networks. The student network is trained on unlabeled data using pseudo-labels generated by the teacher network, while the exam network functions as a temporal ensemble of the student network to stabilize performance. The teacher network is formulated as a joint regression and classification model: the regression branch predicts height values that serve as pseudo-labels, and the classification branch predicts height value classes along with class probabilities, which are used to filter pseudo-labels. Height value classes are defined using a novel Hierarchical Bi-Cut (HBC) strategy to address the inherent long-tailed distribution of heights, and the predicted class probabilities are calibrated with a Plackett-Luce model to reflect the expected accuracy of pseudo-labels. We evaluate the proposed pipeline on three datasets spanning different resolutions and imaging modalities: the ISPRS Vaihingen dataset (IR-R-G aerial images, 0.09 m resolution), the SynRS3D dataset (synthetic images, 0.6–1 m resolution), and the GBH dataset (satellite RGB images, 3 m resolution). Experimental results demonstrate that our approach outperforms supervised and semi-supervised baselines in low-label regimes, and ablation studies confirm the contribution and dataset-dependent behavior of each design component. Code is available at https://github.com/zhu-xlab/tse-net . • First self-training-based semi-supervised learning pipeline for monocular height estimation. • Teacher-Student-Exam pipeline with classification-regression teacher. • Hierarchical Bi-Cut reduces long-tailed biases in height predictions. • Plackett-Luce model aligns pseudo-label reliability with class confidence. • Up to 29.07% gap reduction between 100% and 0.1% labeled data.

title: From articles to canopies: Knowledge-driven pseudo-labelling for tree species classification using LLM experts
summary: Hyperspectral tree species classification is challenging due to limited and imbalanced class labels, spectral mixing (overlapping light signatures from multiple species), and ecological heterogeneity (variability among ecological systems). Addressing these challenges requires methods that integrate biological and structural characteristics of vegetation, such as canopy architecture and interspecific interactions, rather than relying solely on spectral signatures. This paper presents a biologically informed, semi-supervised deep learning method that integrates multi-sensor Earth observation data, specifically hyperspectral imaging (HSI) and airborne laser scanning (ALS), with expert, ecological knowledge. The approach relies on biologically inspired pseudo-labelling over a precomputed canopy graph, yielding improved classification with a lightweight classifier. In addition, ecological priors are constructed using an LLM-assisted, citation-constrained workflow and encoded as a cohabitation matrix with likelihoods of species occurring together. These priors are incorporated into the pseudo-labelling strategy, effectively introducing expert knowledge into the model. Experiments on two real-world forest datasets showed macro-F1 improvements of 6.01 and 4.85 percentage points over the strongest classical HSI--ALS reference pipelines.

title: Heterogeneous SAR–optical fusion for near-real-time land use and land cover mapping under cloud contamination: A novel framework and global benchmark dataset
summary: Optical remote sensing imagery is frequently degraded by cloud and cloud-shadow contamination, which limits its reliability for near-real-time land use and land cover (LULC) mapping. Although synthetic aperture radar (SAR) can provide cloud-penetrating structural information, existing SAR-optical fusion methods often assume reliable optical observations and insufficiently address the semantic uncertainty introduced by cloud contamination. To address this issue, we propose CloudLULC-Net, an end-to-end heterogeneous SAR-optical fusion framework that directly predicts LULC maps from cloud-contaminated Sentinel-2 imagery and temporally adjacent Sentinel-1 SAR observations. The proposed network incorporates optical reliability modulation to suppress unreliable optical responses, heterogeneous information adaptive aggregation to model high-order spatial-channel interactions between optical and SAR representations, and a unified semantic mapping transformer to organize fused features in a LULC-oriented latent space. A semantic anchor-guided optimization strategy is further introduced to improve the consistency of intermediate semantic representations. To support this task, we construct CloudLULC-Set, a large-scale benchmark dataset containing 40,223 curated SAR-optical-label triplets with pixel-level LULC annotations across diverse geographic regions and cloud conditions. Experimental results show that CloudLULC-Net achieves an OA of 86.60%, an F1-score of 83.29%, and an mIoU of 73.51%, outperforming representative heterogeneous reconstruction-first and end-to-end SAR-optical mapping methods. Comparisons with existing global LULC products and analyses under different cloud-cover levels further demonstrate the robustness and practical value of CloudLULC-Net for target-date LULC mapping in cloud-prone regions.The project is publicly available at: https://github.com/RSIIPAC/CloudLULC

title: A prototype-based metric-learning model for sea-ice type mapping from Sentinel-1 SAR and ancillary data
summary: Limited labeled data remains a central challenge for deep-learning-based sea-ice type mapping, while cross-channel relationships remain underexploited, and interaction mechanisms are lacking. This study proposes ESICM, combining Sentinel-1 SAR, AMSR2 brightness temperatures, and ERA5 environmental variables for pixel-level mapping of open water (OW), young ice (YI), first-year ice (FYI), and multi-year ice (MYI). ESICM adopts prototype-based metric learning to fully exploit labels, incorporates a channel multiplication-division module to enhance cross-channel interactions, and introduces two interaction functions, supports-input selection and user dense prompts, to improve classification in hard-to-classify scenes. On the AI4Arctic dataset, trained on 492 AI4Arctic scenes and tested on 20 scenes, ESICM achieved 93.34% overall accuracy, 93.08% F1 score (F1), 88.40% Kappa coefficient, and 77.29% mean intersection over union, exceeding the second-best results by 0.85%–1.55%. Under challenging melt-affected conditions, MYI F1 and intersection over union exceeded the second-best results by 3.13% and 3.93%. Across forward-temporal, cross-region, reduced-training-data, and cross-dataset experiments, ESICM ranked first for 14 and second for two of 16 metrics, indicating relatively strong generalization. In two hard-to-classify scenes, simulated user prompts covering 10% of valid pixels improved all four metrics by more than 4% and 20% over prompt-free inference, respectively, supporting the technical feasibility of interaction. SHAP attributions were broadly consistent with established sea-ice remote-sensing knowledge, enhancing the model’s post hoc interpretability. Overall, ESICM improved sea-ice mapping with limited labeled data and showed application potential under controlled distribution shifts and simulated interaction.

title: Dynamically Weighted Fusion of Daily Multi-Source Precipitation Products over the Haihe River Basin Using a Physically Constrained Two-Stage Framework
summary: Daily precipitation estimates over the Haihe River Basin show strong terrain-related error contrasts. We developed a regional two-stage post-processing fusion workflow for five gridded precipitation products. Physically constrained XGBoost-Tweedie regression uses non-negativity and an archive-derived MaxPrec reference to generate a bias-corrected candidate, ENS_Reg. Dynamic Classification Probability Weighting (DCPW) then uses classifier softmax outputs to weight ENS_Reg and the five original products, producing ENS_RegCla. Models were developed using 2000–2018 data and evaluated on 357,134 station-day records from 2019 to 2023. With the original 1961–2022 MaxPrec reference, ENS_RegCla achieved MAE = 1.064 mm/day, RMSE = 4.807 mm/day, R2 = 0.666, and KGE = 0.746. MAE was 12.6–15.3% lower than for the evaluated equal-weight, inverse-error, and neighborhood error-variance weighting baselines. At a 0.1 mm/day threshold, CSI = 0.653 and HSS = 0.720 exceeded the two specified ablations. Grouped RMSE favored the ablations, whereas grouped MAE differences were not robust. Restricting MaxPrec to 1961–2018 retained better MAE, RMSE, and KGE than all five original products. However, CSI/HSS fell to 0.633/0.698, approximately matching GSMaP-Gauge in CSI but falling below its HSS. The event-skill advantage over the ablation without MaxPrec nearly disappeared, indicating strong dependence on the reference period. Full-sample evaluation included both training and temporal-evaluation periods and yielded pooled MAE = 0.677 mm/day and KGE = 0.783. Of the 2,004,598 full-sample records, 1,647,464 (82.2%) were from model development. GTCH provided an assumption-limited relative-uncertainty diagnostic; the lower minimum statistic after candidate-set expansion was interpreted descriptively, without establishing true uncertainty reduction. Candidate errors may be correlated because ENS_Reg is derived from the original products. The framework supports condition-aware regional precipitation reconstruction, while moderate and heavy rainfall remain priorities for refinement.

title: FSLA-RTDETR: An Improved Four-Scale RT-DETR Network for Dense Small-Object Seabed Pockmark Detection in Shaded-Relief Bathymetric Imagery
summary: Seabed pockmarks are important geomorphological indicators of shallow fluid migration, shallow gas activity, and gas hydrate-related processes. However, automatic pockmark detection from shaded-relief bathymetric imagery remains challenging because many pockmarks have small image-space footprints, occur densely, have weak boundaries, and are embedded in complex seabed backgrounds. To address these issues, this study proposes FSLA-RTDETR, an improved four-scale RT-DETR network for dense small-object seabed pockmark detection. The model introduces SAC-C2f to enhance high-level feature representation, the LPEA Encoder to improve global contextual modeling, and a DGCST-based bidirectional feature fusion network to integrate shallow spatial details and deep semantic information. In addition, the high-resolution P2 feature is incorporated into the decoder to improve small-object localization. A pockmark detection dataset was constructed from publicly available BOEM bathymetric data from the northern Gulf of Mexico, containing 880 images and 8013 annotated pockmark instances. Experimental results show that FSLA-RTDETR achieves mAP50, mAP75, and mAP50–95 values of 0.9218, 0.6221, and 0.5485, respectively. Compared with the baseline RT-DETR, mAP75 and mAP50–95 increase by 6.01 and 2.22 percentage points, respectively. Under the present no-pretraining setting, comparative experiments further demonstrate that FSLA-RTDETR achieves superior high-IoU localization performance compared with the representative object detection models evaluated in this study, providing an effective method for automatic seabed pockmark detection and geomorphological mapping.

title: Application of Multi-Temporal LiDAR for Gully Erosion Monitoring in Mediterranean Intensive Olive Groves
summary: Monitoring the dynamics of gullies in Mediterranean agrosystems is critical but severely limited by agricultural practices that generate continuous machinery compaction and tillage of the soil, camouflaging topographic features and disturbing erosion analyses. This study discusses strategies to quantify erosion by distinguishing natural erosion from agricultural disturbance, integrating multitemporal LiDAR data (2014, 2020, 2024) with gully inventories using orthophoto maps (2011–2022). The volumetric changes were assessed using DoD for the periods 2014–2020 and 2020–2024, and the morphometric performance of the TNO index was further validated using ROC curves in R. Both approaches performed consistently higher in detecting permanent gullies. The TNO index has proven its usefulness for semi-automated delimitation in large or low-data areas. By intersecting DoD surfaces with the gully inventory, localized erosion processes were successfully isolated from the surrounding agricultural landscape matrix. The quantified rate of erosion in the gullies refers strictly to their internal dynamics, which have been close to the natural threshold for soil formation, indicating a risk of soil degradation.

title: Seasonal and Elevational Variations of Forest Greenness in Changbai Mountain During 2000–2024
summary: Mountain forest greenness varies across seasons, yet growing-season averages can mask season-specific relationships with climate variability. We assessed seasonal and elevational variation in historical forest greenness within areas classified as forest in 2024, temporal variation in spring NDVI–climate relationships, and the association between nighttime light (NTL) intensity and forest greenness in Changbai Mountain from 2000 to 2024. We used MODIS-derived normalized difference vegetation index (NDVI), 1 km temperature and precipitation datasets, elevation zones, and annual nighttime light (NTL) data. We applied a forest mask derived from the 2024 Annual China Land Cover Dataset (CLCD) and retained 1 km pixels with at least 70% forest cover. NDVI increased significantly over the aggregate growing season (slope = 0.0011 NDVI yr−1, R2 = 0.584, p < 0.001), summer (slope = 0.0006 NDVI yr−1, R2 = 0.188, p = 0.030), and autumn (slope = 0.0019 NDVI yr−1, R2 = 0.280, p = 0.007). Autumn showed the largest estimated slope; this ranking alone does not establish statistical differences among seasonal slopes. Spring showed no significant long-term trend (slope = 0.0011 NDVI yr−1, R2 = 0.087, p = 0.152), but spring NDVI showed a strong positive correlation with temperature at the regional scale (r = 0.760, p < 0.001), with positive correlations maintained across all elevation zones. In spring regression models, temperature showed a larger standardized coefficient magnitude than precipitation across elevation zones, with all variance inflation factors ≤ 1.22. Exploratory five-year sliding-window correlations suggested temporal variation in spring NDVI–climate relationships, although each estimate was based on only five annual observations. At low elevation, the NTL–NDVI regression was significant (R2 = 0.198, p = 0.026), whereas associations at middle and high elevations were not statistically significant; this raw association should be interpreted cautiously because both variables may contain concurrent temporal trends. These results describe seasonal and elevational greenness patterns within the 2024 forest mask, highlighting the distinct spring temperature association and elevation-dependent relationships between NTL intensity and forest greenness.

title: PRIWCD: Prototype, Relation, and Instance Guidance for Weakly Supervised Remote Sensing Change Detection
summary: Weakly supervised remote sensing change detection reduces annotation costs but suffers from incomplete class activation maps, unreliable pseudo-label propagation, and insufficient discrimination between adjacent change regions. To address these limitations, we propose PRIWCD, a weakly supervised framework for remote sensing change detection. PRIWCD introduces a dynamic prototype comparison module to enhance high-level differential features by modeling unchanged regions and diverse change patterns with multiple dynamic prototypes. A dual relationship propagation guidance module further refines class activation maps by jointly exploiting changes in bi-temporal attention relationships and feature similarity. In addition, instance separation regularization improves feature compactness within pseudo-instances and enhances the separation between changed regions and the background. Experiments on WHU-CD, CLCD, and DSIFN demonstrate the effectiveness of PRIWCD. The proposed method achieves the best mean F1 scores of 79.10%, 62.33%, and 62.68%, respectively, outperforming the compared weakly supervised methods. The results demonstrate that PRIWCD effectively improves pseudo-label quality and provides robust change detection under image-level supervision.

title: Cloud Base Height Inversion Based on a Heterogeneous Stacked Integrated Network
summary: To address the challenge of accurately inverting cloud base height (CBH) from passive remote sensing, this study proposes Hetero-CBHNet, a heterogeneous stacked integrated network framework for CBH inversion. The framework uses random forest (RF), convolutional neural network (CNN), and Transformer models as a pool of candidate base models and employs the RidgeCV algorithm to automatically learn the fusion weights. A total of 1,011,620 samples from FY-4A and MODIS, covering the period from May 2019 to May 2020, were selected (with CloudSat/CALIPSO 2B-CLDCLASS-LIDAR as the ground truth), and the dataset was split chronologically. Across the two data sources under the chronological splitting protocol, Hetero-CBHNet achieves RMSE values of 2966.12 m and 2797.64 m and R values of 0.630 and 0.659 on the test sets, outperforming the individual models. Feature analysis shows that incorporating operational passive cloud type products does not yield a stable gain, indicating that current passive cloud type information is not yet sufficient to replace active satellite labels. In addition, the RMSE values under the random splitting protocol are 1510.01 m and 1488.41 m, substantially better than those under chronological splitting, which confirms the strong dependence of the conclusions on the evaluation protocol.

title: Long-Term Evaluation of AIRS Precipitable Water Vapor over China (2005–2025): Moisture-State-Dependent Bias and Temporal Consistency
summary: Long-term satellite precipitable water vapor (PWV) records are widely used in climate studies, but excellent monthly agreement does not necessarily imply equivalent long-term climate-record consistency. We evaluated Atmospheric Infrared Sounder (AIRS) Version 7 Level-3 monthly PWV against Integrated Global Radiosonde Archive Version 2 (IGRA2) observations at 76 Chinese stations during 2005–2025, using 19,053 matched station-months. The overall agreement was high (R = 0.984, bias = −1.34 mm, RMSE = 3.36 mm). Nevertheless, station-by-calendar-month leave-one-year-out anomalies showed a robust moisture-state dependence of AIRS–IGRA differences (Spearman ρ = −0.722; 95% CI −0.741 to −0.704). The AIRS-on-IGRA OLS anomaly-response slope was 0.473; equal-variance Deming regression increased it to 0.560 (95% CI 0.519–0.596), still below unity. The ascending-minus-descending monthly PWV averaged +0.561 mm and was largest in summer. The network annual bias became more negative at −0.141 mm yr−1, compared with −0.138 mm yr−1 for a strict 73-station fixed network, while the annual R had no significant trend. The station-scale trend consistency was moderate (Pearson r = 0.545; sign agreement 65.8%). An independent BJFS GNSS comparison supported an AIRS contribution to local divergence, but did not establish nationwide attribution. These findings support monthly PWV climatology and broad variability applications over China while showing that small long-term trends require independent constraints, reference-record homogenization, and explicit attention to sampling stability.

title: From Electrification to Urban Nighttime Radiance: Using VIIRS Nighttime Lights to Interpret Progress and Trade-Offs Across Sustainable Development Goals 3, 7, and 11
summary: Nighttime light (NTL) remote sensing provides a globally consistent means of observation of human activity after dark, but its sustainability meaning is context dependent. This study analyzes annual VIIRS Day/Night Band nighttime-light radiance for 467 urban centers from 2015 to 2023 using the same 2015 Global Human Settlement Layer urban-center boundary for every year. Holding the spatial footprint constant provides an apples-to-apples longitudinal comparison: changes in Sum VNL represent changes in satellite-observed radiance within the same geographic area rather than changes caused by expanding or redefining the urban boundary. Across the 467 fixed urban areas, total Sum VNL increased from 7.43 million in 2015 to 8.51 million in 2023 (+14.49%); 374 cities increased and 93 decreased. The sample declined by 2.49% from 2019 to 2020 and increased by 5.44% from 2020 to 2021. Regional 2015–2023 changes were +27.96% in Asia, +16.17% in Africa, +14.78% in Oceania, +11.69% in Latin America and the Caribbean, +3.73% in Northern America, and −1.96% in Europe. Mean VNL is reported alongside Sum VNL to distinguish average radiance intensity from total radiance within each fixed urban footprint. The results demonstrate substantial spatial and temporal heterogeneity but do not by themselves prove energy poverty, over-illumination, electricity consumption, or health exposure. NTL is therefore interpreted as a complementary diagnostic variable for SDGs 3, 7, and 11 that requires contextual validation.

title: A 1 km Monthly Multi-Timescale SPEI Dataset for Mainland China Reconstructed from Station Observations and Multi-Source Environmental Predictors
summary: High-resolution multi-timescale SPEI data are important for drought monitoring and climate-impact studies, but long-term high-resolution datasets remain limited over large regions. This study developed and technically validated a station-supervised monthly multi-timescale SPEI dataset for mainland China from 1979 to 2018 on a 1 km grid, including SPEI-1, SPEI-3, SPEI-6, SPEI-12, and SPEI-24. Monthly labels were extracted from daily records at 427 stations using an exact source-calendar month-end rule. Monthly 0.1° CMFD predictors were mapped to stations and 1 km pixel centres using a NaN-aware bilinear sampler and combined with complete-window temporal features and NASADEM terrain covariates. Five timescale-specific LightGBM models generated 2359 nationwide monthly rasters. Random five-fold cross-validation yielded mean R2 values of 0.8807–0.9122; 200 km spatial-block validation with a 100 km exclusion buffer yielded 0.7857–0.8739; and forward blocked-period validation yielded 0.7577–0.8337. Full-period product comparison gave Pearson r = 0.9295 against Zhang-SPEI for SPEI-3, while comparison with HSPEI across five timescales yielded r = 0.7772–0.3267. Spatially buffered drought-condition validation produced F1 scores of 0.7021–0.7838 for moderate-or-worse drought, whereas extreme-drought Recall was 0.2397–0.3869. The dataset provides a long-term, multi-timescale resource for drought monitoring and climate-impact research across mainland China, with validation results characterizing its performance across regions, periods, and drought-severity levels.

title: Aerosol Optical and Microphysical Characteristics Related to Vertical Distribution over Korea Using Aerosol Scale Height
summary: Aerosol optical depth characterizes total aerosol loading in the atmospheric column but does not directly indicate its vertical distribution relative to the planetary boundary layer. This study investigates aerosol vertical structure over Daejeon, Korea, by integrating column aerosol optical properties from a sky radiometer, near-surface atmospheric extinction measurements, and planetary boundary layer height from reanalysis data. Aerosol scale height is derived from aerosol optical depth at 870 nm and near-surface extinction and is analyzed alongside aerosol optical and microphysical properties. Aerosol scale height exhibits substantial variability relative to the planetary boundary layer height, with the highest relative values occurring in spring and the lowest in autumn. An increase in aerosol scale height relative to the boundary layer is accompanied by a decrease in the Ångström exponent and an increase in the coarse-mode volume fraction. The coarse-mode enhancement is driven mainly by an increase in coarse-mode aerosol volume, whereas surface PM10 concentrations show only a weak relationship with variations in vertical structure. Single scattering albedo generally increases, indicating a more scattering dominated column aerosol population. These results demonstrate that combining aerosol scale height with planetary boundary layer height provides valuable information on aerosol vertical structure and the degree of correspondence between surface and column aerosol conditions.

title: A Dual-Branch Framework Combining Amplitude and Phase Information for SAR Sea Ice Classification
summary: Sea ice detection and classification are critical for navigation safety and climate change research. With its high-resolution, all-weather, and day-and-night imaging capabilities, Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) has become a vital data source for these tasks. However, most existing deep learning studies rely on amplitude data, failing to fully exploit complex-valued information. This study evaluates whether locally filtered inter-channel phase information from Sentinel-1 Single Look Complex (SLC) data provides complementary information to conventional HH and HV amplitudes. Using the AI4 Arctic Sea Ice Challenge Dataset (ASID Challenge), we construct a complex-valued dataset and evaluate different input combinations with four representative semantic segmentation networks. We examine the classification results across six different categories in the ASID Challenge and, in conjunction with real navigation scenarios, map these six categories into three classes: Open Water, Early-stage Ice, and Developed Ice. For FCN under direct three-class training, phase augmentation improved the mean test Macro-F1 and mIoU by 4.4% and 6.1%. The results show that although its benefit is not consistent across all six-class classification experiments, phase information provides more reliable improvements when sea ice types are grouped according to broader development stages. These findings suggest that inter-channel phase contains complementary information beyond amplitude and may improve SAR sea ice classification under practical application scenarios.

title: UAV-Based Hyperspectral Monitoring of Foliar Nitrogen in Spinach (Spinacia oleracea L.): Comparing Flight-Specific, Window-Based, and Time-Integrated Modeling Approaches
summary: Spinach (Spinacia oleracea L.) is an economically important leafy vegetable whose nitrogen management remains comparatively understudied with remote sensing tools relative to major row crops. This study evaluated the potential of unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV)-based hyperspectral imagery to estimate foliar nitrogen content (%N) in field-grown spinach at a commercial plot across two growing seasons and four nitrogen fertilization treatments. Nine spectral indices were related to destructively measured %N at four phenological stages of the Biologische Bundesanstalt, Bundessortenamt und CHemische Industrie (BBCH) scale (BBCH 16, 30, 45, and 49) under three modeling scenarios, ranging from flight-specific regression to a continuous model incorporating days after sowing (DAS) as a proxy for crop development, with model performance assessed out-of-sample by repeated cross-validation. Foliar nitrogen content differed significantly among treatments from BBCH 30 onward and only marginally at the earliest stage, with the two highest doses converging into a statistically indistinguishable class. The Vogelmann red-edge index 3 (VOGREI3) yielded the most accurate estimates, peaking at BBCH 45 (cross-validated coefficient of determination, R2 = 0.845) before declining significantly at BBCH 49, a loss consistent with spectral saturation of the closed canopy. A single continuous model incorporating DAS covered the BBCH 45 and BBCH 49 flights with a relative error of 12.4%, against 9.6% and 14.9% for the corresponding flight-specific models, and required no stage-specific recalibration within the calibration seasons. In an unseen season, plot ranking was preserved, and a few reference samples corrected the bias. UAV hyperspectral imagery combined with development-stage-aware modeling therefore shows potential for non-destructive nitrogen monitoring in spinach once locally calibrated, although transferability across further seasons, sites and cultivars remains to be established.

title: A Feature-Fusion Convolutional Neural Network for Terrain Generalization
summary: Terrain generalization—the scale-driven abstraction of digital elevation models (DEMs) that retains dominant landforms while filtering trivial microtopography—has long been dominated by rule-based algorithms, whereas deep learning has mainly targeted the inverse task of DEM super-resolution. This study proposes TG-CNN, a feature-fusion convolutional neural network for DEM down-scaling generalization. The network compresses the high-resolution DEM through a max- or average-pooling front end, combines normalized elevation with slope and sine–cosine circularly encoded aspect as complementary input channels, and is trained with a composite elevation–slope–aspect loss. Training, validation, and testing are conducted on geographically independent mountainous areas under a leave-one-area-out scheme, followed by adjustable IDW fusion post-processing. On the test region, classical bilinear interpolation retains the best elevation accuracy, while the standalone TG-CNN does not reach a comparable level; fused accuracy improves monotonically as the IDW share increases, indicating that the fusion benefit originates from the interpolation component. On the ridge–valley structure, however, TG-CNN behaves as an aggressive yet reliable filter: it achieves the highest precision and the smallest positional offset among all compared methods but retains only part of the reference skeleton, leaving its F1-score below the interpolation baseline. TG-CNN thus realizes a genuine, controllable terrain-abstraction effect, yet deep learning does not yet surpass mature interpolation in pixel-level elevation accuracy—a negative result that clarifies current limitations and points toward residual learning and information-preserving architectures.

title: SENSERO: A Multi-Scale, Multi-Label Sentinel-2 Benchmark for Romania with Cross-Scale Land-Cover Classification Baselines
summary: Patch size is an important design parameter in patch-based Earth observation (EO) learning, yet it is rarely treated as an experimental variable because existing benchmarks use a single fixed scale. We introduce SENSERO, a multi-scale, multi-label Sentinel-2 benchmark for Romania consisting of 10,000 geographically fixed locations extracted at eight patch sizes, from 64×64 to 336×336 pixels, at a constant 10 m ground sampling distance, so that all scales share identical patch centres and an identical, spatially disjoint 70/15/15 partition. Each patch provides twelve-band bottom-of-atmosphere reflectance, a rasterised CORINE Land Cover (CLC) 2018 reference map from which five deterministic multi-label annotation layers are derived (three levels of the CLC hierarchy, the BigEarthNet nomenclature, and a scheme adapted to the Romanian landscape). The benchmark task is patch-level multi-label classification; the rasterised reference maps serve to derive and trace the labels, not as a segmentation target. Using ResNet-50 baselines trained from scratch, we find that larger patches bring little benefit at CLC Level 1 but clear gains at Levels 2 and 3 (macro mAP at Level 3 rising from 0.42 at 64 px to 0.61 at 336 px), with per-location gains saturating around 224–256 pixels; that transfer across scales is asymmetric, models trained on wide patches transferring to narrow ones far better than the reverse; and that the choice of nomenclature affects measured performance as much as patch size. Leave-scene-out cross-validation, an ablation of the labelling rule, pretrained ResNet-50 and ViT-S/16 controls and bootstrap confidence intervals show that the scale effect is not attributable to spatial leakage, to the annotation rule, or to the baseline architecture. Comparison with an independent 10 m land-cover product shows that the gain from context is concentrated where CLC labels generalise over heterogeneous ground.

title: Dynamic Landslide Susceptibility Assessment Using a PRSU Strategy and SBAS-InSAR Technology
summary: Reconciling high-resolution statistical modeling with geomorphologically meaningful management units remains a challenge in landslide susceptibility assessment. Focusing on the landslide-prone Three Gorges Reservoir area in central China, this study evaluates a framework with three components: (i) a systematic evaluation of statistical metrics (mean, median, standard deviation, range, and IQR for continuous features; mode for categorical features) for feature upscaling within slope units; (ii) a comparative analysis between direct slope-unit modeling (Pixel Feature-to-Slope Unit, PFSU) and a strategy mapping pixel-level predictions to slope units (Pixel Result-to-Slope Unit, PRSU); and (iii) the integration of active deformation monitoring using 166 scenes of Sentinel-1A SBAS-InSAR data (2019–2025). PRSU-Q75-Stacking, combining Stacking with the 75th percentile (Q75) aggregation method, had the highest reported slope-unit AUC in the original evaluation. Coupling the selected susceptibility baseline with InSAR-derived deformation indicators produced a deformation-informed classification that may help prioritize field investigation and monitoring.

title: Temporally Integrated MODIS NDVI and Simulated Cumulative Biomass in Mediterranean Grasslands
summary: Mediterranean grasslands exhibit strong seasonality, complicating comparisons between satellite-derived vegetation greenness and cumulative biomass production. This study examined how temporal integration and segmentation influence the association between the MODIS Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) and cumulative biomass production simulated by the SIMPAST ecohydrological model. MODIS NDVI time series (MOD09Q1; eight-day composites; 250 m) spanning 2000–2025 were analysed at three grassland sites in central Spain. Non-accumulated NDVI and two cumulative metrics, based on simple and conditional accumulation, were compared with simulated production under conventional seasons and five fixed eco-phenological periods. Simulations used six original meteorological forcing trajectories and an additional forcing dataset based on observed weather. The temporally matched reference relationship between non-accumulated NDVI and simulated eight-day biomass production yielded mean R2 values of 0.188, 0.069, and 0.073 at Piñuecar, Colmenar Viejo, and Tielmes, respectively. Pooled relationships between cumulative NDVI and cumulative simulated biomass were substantially stronger (R2 = 0.714–0.746 for simple accumulation and 0.600–0.723 for conditional accumulation), although these higher values partly reflected their shared within-year temporal progression. Observed meteorological forcing showed the same general pattern, with interval-level reference R2 values of 0.122–0.263 and substantially stronger pooled relationships for the cumulative metrics. However, first differencing reduced mean R2 for simple accumulation to 0.180 at Piñuecar, 0.004 at Colmenar Viejo, and 0.097 at Tielmes, indicating that the strong cumulative associations depended partly on shared within-year progression. Conventional seasons generally yielded the strongest associations in autumn or spring, whereas eco-phenological segmentation generally concentrated them in winter-to-early spring growth. Neither eco-phenological segmentation nor conditional accumulation consistently increased R2 relative to its alternative. These findings distinguish correspondence between cumulative seasonal trajectories from associations at individual observation intervals. Temporal segmentation provides a complementary interpretative framework, but high cumulative R2 values do not establish predictive performance. Operational applications require independent field evaluation of whether these indicators capture biomass production variability beyond shared seasonal progression.

title: Event-Based and Error-Component Evaluation of GPM IMERG and GSMaP_Gauge for Monitoring Hourly Extreme Precipitation over North China
summary: Hourly satellite precipitation products are often evaluated using aggregate statistics that can conceal compensating errors in precipitation occurrence and event duration, accumulation, and intensity. Using all matched observations from 522 meteorological stations in North China between 1 October 2019 and 26 September 2022, this study evaluated GPM IMERG Final Run V07 and GSMaP_Gauge V8. The framework combined precipitation-amount and occurrence metrics, event characteristics defined using local 90th percentiles of wet-hour precipitation, and additive and multiplicative error decomposition. IMERG showed a persistent dry bias, with a mean annualized total error of −348.2 mm yr−1. GSMaP had a higher probability of detection than IMERG (77.6% versus 38.6%) but also a higher false alarm ratio (67.5% versus 29.7%); its mean total error of +99.7 mm yr−1 masked substantial compensation among the error components. For extreme precipitation events, IMERG underestimated annualized event frequency by 33.9% but reproduced mean duration comparatively closely (−11.0%). GSMaP overestimated event frequency by 31.6% and duration by 198.6%. Its near-unbiased mean event total (+1.1%) resulted from prolonged duration despite underestimation of mean and peak intensity by 67.3% and 67.4%, respectively. Within the approximately three-year evaluation period examined here, these results show that product selection should be application-specific and that event-scale correction should address precipitation occurrence, duration, accumulation, and intensity jointly.

title: GUF-Net: Gated Uncertainty-Aware Fusion Network for Robust Building Change Detection in Remote Sensing Images
summary: Building change detection (BCD) in high-resolution remote sensing imagery has achieved considerable accuracy with deep learning, yet most existing models still suffer from performance degradation under noise interference, partly due to inadequate uncertainty handling. To address this, we propose GUF-Net, a gated uncertainty-aware fusion network that integrates three key components: (1) a pixel-wise uncertainty modeling module that generates a pixel-level uncertainty map alongside the change probability map; (2) an adaptive gated fusion mechanism that dynamically weights multi-scale features and uncertainty information; and (3) a redesigned loss function that can directly supervise the uncertainty estimation, ensuring that it reflects prediction reliability rather than serving as an unsupervised auxiliary output. Experiments on three public benchmarks (WHU-CD, CDD, and LEVIR-CD) show that GUF-Net achieves competitive F1 scores of 93.88%, 96.55%, and 90.43%, respectively, ranking top three on CDD and WHU-CD, while its advantage is less pronounced on LEVIR-CD. Under the strongest Gaussian, salt-and-pepper, and speckle noise conditions on the WHU-CD test set, the F1 score of GUF-Net decreases by only 0.86, 3.95, and 1.29 percentage points, respectively, exhibiting the smallest degradation among the compared models. Unlike existing uncertainty-aware baselines evaluated solely on clean data, GUF-Net jointly supervises evidential pixel uncertainty and routes it through adaptive gating, enabling stable fusion under degraded imaging conditions. Ablation studies confirm that the gated fusion, uncertainty injection, and global context aggregation each contribute to the overall performance. These results suggest that explicit uncertainty modeling and adaptive fusion can improve the reliability of BCD under noisy conditions, although there remains room for further improvement in clean-set accuracy and model efficiency.

title: UniRS-Seg: Shared Sparse–Dense Query Decoding for Joint Semantic and Referring Remote Sensing Segmentation
summary: Remote sensing semantic and referring segmentation share mask geometry but differ in whether a category vocabulary or a natural-language expression selects the output. UniRS-Seg bridges these interfaces through a shared sparse–dense query compiler and a hierarchical mask decoder, jointly trained on independently annotated datasets. Class names and referring expressions are projected from SigLIP 2 into the same decoder space; dense image–query activations supply spatial support, and sparse query tokens specify the requested region. An adapted SAM ViT-B pathway and parallel convolutional features recover local geometry, while learnable soft mask cross-attention refines both tasks and class-balanced mask-guided self-attention supports semantic parsing. UniRS-Seg achieves 57.30%, 85.31%, and 88.24% mIoU on LoveDA, Vaihingen, and Potsdam, and 78.18% and 70.88% gIoU on RefSegRS and RRSIS-D. These scores exceed the strongest listed baseline means by 0.68, 0.99, 1.18, 0.79, and 1.71 percentage points, respectively. Against separately trained semantic-only and referring-only versions of the shared architecture, joint training improves the four evaluated datasets by 0.45, 0.89, 1.40, and 0.97 points. An additional supervised RISBench evaluation achieves 72.91% gIoU and 74.85% cIoU, with the highest gIoU among the listed methods. On RefSegRS, adding learnable mask cross-attention to combined sparse and dense prompts increases gIoU by 0.86 points. The results support supervised dual-task transfer through a common query-conditioned decoder; the comparison uses published baseline results and does not establish unseen-domain or zero-shot generalization.

title: Sparse VLF/LF Lightning Location: Propagation Correction and Accelerating-Charge-Based Peak-Field Consistency
summary: Sparse very-low-frequency/low-frequency (VLF/LF) lightning location is a ground-based passive remote-sensing technique, but sparse station geometry and finite-conductivity propagation can shift peak arrival times, alter peak amplitudes, and produce spurious solutions. This study proposes a three-station method integrating propagation correction with accelerating charge method (ACM)-based peak-electric-field consistency. Based on the Liénard–Wiechert field, the ACM relates the radiation field to charge acceleration and assumes a common source-side peak for the same return stroke. For given ground conductivity, relative permittivity, and an ACM reference field, the range-dependent additional delay τE corrects TDOA to obtain candidate locations. After candidate coordinates are fixed, the peak-retention factor AE, candidate-to-station distances, and local response Ki recover equivalent source-side peaks, while Jamp discriminates between correct and spurious candidates. In simulations, the in-network location error decreased from 46.0 to 21.8 m and the out-of-network error from 1867.3 to 394.8 m; the ACM-based criterion selected the correct candidate in both cases. For the S7–S8–S9 rocket-triggered-lightning case, the near-candidate error decreased from 1.333 to 0.360 km, and Jamp values of 0.0419 and 0.2238 distinguished the correct and spurious solutions. The method therefore improves sparse VLF/LF lightning location accuracy through propagation-time correction and supports spurious-solution discrimination through propagation-corrected peak-field consistency.

title: A Decadal Total Suspended Solids Dataset for China’s Coastal Waters Reconstructed from Sentinel-2 Imagery Using a Spatiotemporal Graph Neural Network
summary: Total suspended solids (TSS) are a key indicator of coastal water quality and sediment dynamics, yet their long-term spatiotemporal variability remains insufficiently characterized at large spatial scales. In this study, a decade-long (2016–2025) TSS dataset for China’s coastal waters was reconstructed from Sentinel-2 multispectral imagery using a spatiotemporal graph neural network (STGNN-TSS), which integrates graph attention networks with temporal sequence modeling. The model was trained using satellite-derived reference TSS observations and evaluated using spatially separated test samples and comparative experiments. During relatively stable seasonal conditions, STGNN-TSS achieved an R2 of 0.739, an RMSE of 3.924 mg L−1, and an MAE of 1.907 mg L−1 across China’s coastal waters. The reconstructed products for other years showed consistent spatial patterns with independent satellite-derived SPM products, with Spearman correlation coefficients ranging from 0.738 to 0.891. Based on the reconstructed dataset, TSS exhibited a persistent “high-inshore, low-offshore” spatial pattern with pronounced regional differences among northern shallow seas, major estuarine systems, and southern coastal waters. Seasonal variations were identified, characterized by elevated TSS concentrations in winter and reduced concentrations in summer. Interannual variability during 2016–2025 showed an increasing trend before 2020 followed by a general decline, with substantial regional differences in variability intensity. The reconstructed TSS dataset provides a consistent basis for investigating long-term suspended sediment dynamics and supports large-scale coastal environmental monitoring and management.

title: Identifying Cloud Regimes and Their Transitions Related to Extreme Precipitation and Hail Events over the Alps Through Self-Supervised Learning
summary: Extreme precipitation and hail events over complex terrain are strongly dependent on the multiscale evolution of convective systems, yet their development remains challenging to observe and model. In this study, we apply a self-supervised learning (SSL) framework to Meteosat infrared 10.8 μm imagery over the Alpine region to derive physically meaningful representations of convective cloud organization across the full daily cycle. The learned representation organizes convective cloud scenes into three primary regimes: early convection (EC), deep convection (DC), and overcast anvil systems (OA), each exhibiting distinct cloud-top properties, spatial structures, and day–night distributions consistent with established convective development stages. Within the developed SSL framework, reported extreme precipitation and hail events are preferentially associated with these regimes, occupying the upper tail of cloud-top height, optical thickness, and cloud coverage distributions within the latent space. This indicates that extremes correspond to rare, intense realizations of continuous convective variability. Two dominant pathways of cloud structure evolution are identified: a rapid EC→DC transition and a persistent DC mode. The former is characterized by fast cloud growth and intensification, while the latter corresponds to mature convective systems with sustained cloud properties. Overall, the results demonstrate that infrared-based SSL representations capture physically consistent convective stages and their transitions, providing a novel observational framework for characterizing extreme convective events and supporting the evaluation of convection-resolving numerical weather prediction models.

title: ED-iSwinLSTM-ND: A Spatiotemporal Deep Learning Model for Global Ionospheric TEC Forecasting
summary: Accurate forecasting of global ionospheric total electron content (TEC) is important for space weather research and Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) applications. To address the complex spatiotemporal variability of TEC and the artificial discontinuity across the ±180° longitude boundary in global TEC maps, this study proposes an improved SwinLSTM model (iSwinLSTM) and further develops the ED-iSwinLSTM-ND framework for global TEC forecasting. By redesigning the shifted-window mechanism to account for longitudinal periodicity, iSwinLSTM enhances cross-boundary information interaction, while an Encoder–Decoder architecture combined with the Next-Day (ND) strategy enables prediction of the next 12 TEC maps from the preceding 36 maps. The model was evaluated retrospectively using archived GIMs from the selected test years. In 2025, a high solar activity year, the model achieved an MAE of 3.51 TECU, an RMSE of 5.10 TECU, and an R2 of 0.94; in 2020, a low solar activity year, the corresponding values were 0.96 TECU, 1.50 TECU, and 0.95. Boundary experiments further confirmed that the periodic shifted-window mechanism effectively reduces longitude-boundary errors. Overall, ED-iSwinLSTM-ND provides an effective framework for short-term global TEC forecasting by jointly exploiting spatiotemporal dependencies, longitudinal periodicity, and diurnal characteristics.

title: CA-Mamba: A Change-Aware Mamba Decoding Framework for Remote Sensing Binary Change Detection
summary: Remote sensing binary change detection aims to identify real changes in bi-temporal images while suppressing pseudo-change responses induced by complex backgrounds and temporal variations in otherwise unchanged regions. Although existing state-space-based methods incorporate cross-temporal interaction, integrating explicit difference priors into state-space parameter generation and subsequent boundary-aware decoding remains an important design problem. To address this problem, CA-Mamba, a change-aware Mamba decoding framework, is proposed. An Asymmetric Change-Aware State-Space Mixer (ACSSM) is introduced to condition state-space parameter generation on bi-temporal difference priors and to modulate the two temporal branches asymmetrically. The Cascaded Difference Prior Module (CDPM), the Change Boundary Enhancement (CBE) module, and the Change Representation Constructor (CRC) are further integrated into a unified pipeline for difference-prior generation and propagation, change-aware mixing, boundary enhancement, and region–boundary collaborative representation construction. Experiments on four public datasets, namely, LEVIR-CD, WHU-CD, CDD, and CLCD, show competitive detection performance. Ablation results support the use of signed-difference pathways and the overall CRC design under the evaluated settings. The efficiency analysis characterizes the trade-offs among detection accuracy, reported computational cost, inference latency, and parameter storage.

title: PSeq-Net: End-to-End Sparse-Global Sequence Modeling for Bridge Detection in Ultra-High-Resolution Remote Sensing Imagery
summary: Robust bridge detection in ultra-high-resolution remote sensing imagery is important for transportation infrastructure mapping, geographic information system updating, and post-disaster assessment. However, local cropping can interrupt the spatial continuity of long-span bridges, leading to fragmented detections and geometrically inconsistent predictions. This paper proposes a polygon sequence network (PSeq-Net), an end-to-end sparse-global sequence modeling framework for bridge detection in very-high-resolution (VHR) remote sensing imagery. PSeq-Net generates an ordered quadrilateral vertex sequence for each bridge, unifying visual encoding and structured geometric prediction. Hierarchical sparse feature sampling preserves fine-grained evidence in bridge-relevant regions while using compact representations of background areas, enabling efficient processing of 2048 × 2048 inputs. Global context aggregation integrates long-range spatial dependencies, and geometry-aware optimization improves the structural plausibility of predicted bridge shapes. Experiments on the large-scale GLH-Bridge benchmark show that PSeq-Net achieves 37.87% average precision (AP), 73.58% AP50, and 31.38% AP75, outperforming representative oriented and large-scale bridge detectors. Further analyses highlight improved localization of elongated and boundary-crossing bridges, reduced fragmentation, and robustness across diverse scene backgrounds and image resolutions.

title: Mapping Local Climate Zones and Their Long-Term Changes in 105 Major Chinese Cities from 2000 to 2025
summary: Rapid urban growth has transformed the three-dimensional structure and land cover composition of Chinese cities, yet long-term local climate zone (LCZ) changes remain insufficiently resolved at fine spatial scales. We mapped all 17 standard LCZ classes for 105 major Chinese cities in 2000, 2005, 2010, 2015, 2020, and 2025 at a 30 m resolution. A unified random forest framework implemented on Google Earth Engine integrated Landsat imagery with spectral, topographic, building, vegetation, and ancillary land cover information. Overall accuracy ranged from 83.88% to 88.71% across the six mapping years. The mapped urban area increased from 2.14 × 104 to 5.86 × 104 km2, with the strongest relative growth shifting from eastern toward central and western China. Although the built-class area more than doubled, its share declined from 68.61% to 53.27%, while the proportion of vegetated-class area increased from 20.47% to 39.51%. LCZ D, LCZ 9, and LCZ A contributed most to the overall increase, whereas LCZ 8 declined in proportional importance. All moisture regions shifted toward more balanced built–vegetated configurations. Dryland cities, however, retained more bare surfaces and less woody vegetation than humid and transitional cities. These maps reveal both a common national trajectory and climate-conditioned regional differentiation, providing a basis for urban-climate assessment and climate-sensitive planning.

title: Assessing the Reliability of Multi-Source Gridded Precipitation Products for Use as Inputs to Hydrological and Hydroclimatic Applications: A Case Study of the Helmand River Basin, Afghanistan
summary: Reliable precipitation datasets are essential for basin-scale water resources assessment, climate analysis, flood and drought-related studies, whereas estimation remains challenging in arid to semi-arid, topographically complex, and data-scarce regions. This issue is particularly important in the Helmand River Basin (HRB), Afghanistan, where uncertainty in precipitation input can directly affect hydrological and hydroclimatic assessments. This study evaluated eight multi-source gridded precipitation products against gauge observations from 18 hydro-meteorological stations across the HRB. The evaluation covered daily and monthly timescales, wet and dry season conditions, rainfall-event thresholds, and elevation settings using continuous, categorical, and integrated multi-metric analyses. The results indicate that precipitation product performance in the HRB varies with temporal scale, seasonal regime, and elevation setting. In general, monthly and wet-season evaluations showed better agreement than daily and dry-season evaluations; however, this pattern reflects the combined influence of temporal scale, native product resolution, and spatial extraction method. Among the evaluated datasets, MSWEP and ERA5-Land showed the most balanced overall performance, combining better temporal agreement, lower error, lower bias, and higher rainfall-event detection across stations and elevation classes. CHIRPS also performed well, particularly at monthly and seasonal scales, whereas IMERG and PERSIANN-CDR showed moderate performance. Conversely, CMORPH and GPCC Products were the least reliable because of persistent underestimation in the former and inflated variability and overestimation in the latter. The results further indicate that dataset skill is not spatially uniform, with weaker performance generally associated with high-elevation stations. Overall, this study establishes a basin-specific framework for precipitation dataset selection in the HRB and provides a reproducible basis for selecting fit-for-purpose precipitation inputs for future water resources and hydroclimatic studies in this data-scarce region.

title: A Comparative Study of Deep Learning Architectures for Multi-Source Precipitation Data Fusion Towards Daily Precipitation Estimation in the Yellow River Basin, China
summary: Accurate precipitation estimation is crucial for water management and flood reconstructions, yet remains challenging due to sparse ground observations and systematic satellite biases. Despite the rise of deep learning in multi-source fusion, controlled comparisons under a unified framework remain scarce, and the roles of window size and precipitation product combinations remain underexplored. This study evaluated five deep learning architectures, namely 1D CNN, 2D CNN, 1D–2D CNN, 3D CNN, and Transformer, for fusing three precipitation products (IMERG, MSWEP, and ERA5-Land) to estimate station-scale daily precipitation in the Yellow River Basin, China. Results showed that deep learning models consistently outperformed individual products, weighting methods, and machine learning methods, with Transformer achieving the best overall performance, followed by 3D CNN; MSWEP led the standalone products. Spatial improvements were more pronounced in densely gauged areas, but Transformer also performed well in the sparse western regions. All products and fusion models tended to overestimate no-rain and light-rain events and underestimate moderate-to-heavy, and extreme events, with Transformer yielding the largest reductions in conditional RMSE and BIAS for heavy and extreme events. Enlarging the spatial or temporal window individually improved performance, and combining both worked even better. Ablation experiments revealed that IMERG contributed little unique information, whereas incorporating more products generally improved Transformer performance. Overall, Transformer demonstrated superior performance in fusing precipitation products and enhancing estimation accuracy.

title: Rethinking Focus-and-Detect for Aerial Small Object Detection Under a Frozen-Detector Protocol: A Translation-Equivariance-Guided Approach
summary: Objects in unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) imagery are typically small, densely packed, and unevenly distributed. The prevailing focus-and-detect paradigm—first localizing focus regions where objects concentrate, and then performing detection within them—has substantially improved small object detection. Existing focusing modules, however, are almost always coupled with architectural modifications to the detector and with patch-based training, which makes the contribution of the focusing mechanism itself difficult to quantify. More importantly, whether the focusing mechanism alone can yield genuine gains on off-the-shelf detectors without any retraining remains insufficiently examined. To address these issues, we first integrate the focusing modules of several representative open-source methods into frozen detectors, removing the architectural modifications and stripping away the patch-based training on which these modules rely, so as to isolate the genuine gain of the focusing mechanism. We then establish translation equivariance as a design principle for focus-region generation and propose a strictly translation-equivariant heatmap network for this purpose. The resulting focus regions are further processed via super-resolution and image packing to construct focus images that are better suited to frozen detectors. Extensive experiments on VisDrone show that, with a strong baseline, directly plugging existing focusing modules into a frozen detector generally hurts rather than helps; when the baseline is weakened by lowering the input resolution, their gains reappear, but the final accuracy remains substantially below that of the high-resolution baseline. In contrast, our method raises the mean average precision (mAP@0.5:0.95) of multiple strong baseline detectors by 0.44–1.03 points on VisDrone-test-dev, without any retraining. When further combined with patch-based training, the overall framework achieves a total gain of 1.24–2.22 points over the strong baseline.

title: A Lightweight Spectral–Spatial Network for Efficient Semantic Segmentation of Ground-Based Hyperspectral Imagery
summary: Ground-based hyperspectral imaging extends remote sensing to road environments by providing material-sensitive spectra for distinguishing visually similar surfaces and objects. However, pixel-wise prediction from high-dimensional spectral cubes is computationally demanding. This study presents a lightweight spectral–spatial network for efficient semantic segmentation of ground-based hyperspectral imagery. A Spectral Token Stem compresses ordered bands into pooled, normalized, and statistical descriptors before high-resolution encoding. CoordSK blocks combine coordinate-aware directional aggregation with adaptive local-scale selection, while a lightweight guided decoder recovers dense predictions from multi-level features. Experiments on the public HyKo2 and HSI-Drive datasets yield Jaccard indices of 0.6670 and 0.8181, respectively, outperforming representative efficient segmentation baselines. The model contains 0.656 million trainable parameters and reaches FP32 batch-one throughputs of 151.49 and 168.21 FPS on an RTX 5090 for the respective benchmarks. In the additional pretrained-model comparison, the network uses less than 0.5% of HSI-Adapter’s total parameters. Ablation studies validate the contributions of spectral tokenization and coordinate-selective mixing, and an input-representation study demonstrates the benefit of retaining full hyperspectral observations over PCA and pseudo-RGB inputs. These results indicate a favorable accuracy–efficiency trade-off for ground-based hyperspectral remote sensing scene understanding.

title: RLGD: A High-Resolution UAV Dataset and Benchmark for Semantic Segmentation and Revetment Extraction in Waterway Scenes
summary: High-resolution unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) imagery is increasingly used for waterway inspection, but automated scene understanding remains constrained by the lack of pixel-level datasets that explicitly represent revetments and their complex interfaces with water, vegetation, roads, and riverside structures. We introduce the Riverway and Landscape Ground Dataset (RLGD), a dedicated UAV semantic segmentation dataset for waterway scenes. RLGD contains 100 images at 3000×4000 pixels, corresponding to 1.2 billion labeled pixels. Its public RLGD taxonomy explicitly includes revetment. Seven semantic segmentation models are evaluated under a unified protocol. Across five training runs with different random seeds, mean mIoU ranges from 69.27% to 77.02%, while Hierarchical Joint Network with Boundary Guidance (GHJNet) achieves 77.02 ± 0.41% mIoU and 83.51 ± 1.18% revetment IoU. Direct transfer from Varied Drone Dataset (VDD) to RLGD results in relative mIoU reductions of 11.29–49.81%, whereas adaptation using 20% of the RLGD training source images closes 65.5% of the measured domain gap. For the GHJNet run used in the downstream analysis, object-prior refinement using the Segment Anything Model (SAM) increases revetment IoU from 84.10% to 87.25%. A 42-image visual-completeness screening case study further achieves 83.93% macro-F1 and 81.25% balanced accuracy against image-level interpretations by three experts. Overall, RLGD provides a densely annotated, task-specific benchmark for dry-season waterway semantic segmentation, revetment extraction, and image-level inspection prioritization within the surveyed Yangtze River corridor.

title: CPSF-Net: Confidence-Chained Position-Sensitive and Scale-Aware Fusion Network for Visible-Thermal Tiny Ship Detection
summary: Growing demands for maritime security and navigational safety have made video surveillance indispensable for monitoring distant ship targets. Visible-thermal fusion provides a robust solution across varying weather and illumination conditions; however, tiny targets remain highly sensitive to positional errors, and cross-modal misalignment caused by occlusion, low illumination, and cluttered scenes further degrades detection accuracy. To address these issues, we propose CPSF-Net, a confidence-chained, position-sensitive and scale-aware fusion network for visible-thermal tiny ship detection. A Position-Sensitive Multimodal Fusion (PMF) module enhances and fuses pre-aligned visible-thermal features with possible residual local misalignment through cross-attention and derives a position-sensitive token-level matching confidence directly from the attention weights without introducing additional parameters. A Confidence-Guided Sparse Attention (CSA) module uses this confidence to adaptively suppress redundant cross-modal correlations and improve positional awareness. Finally, an adaptive Scale-Weighted Loss (SWL) balances Intersection over Union (IoU) and Normalized Wasserstein Distance (NWD) according to object scale and matching confidence, providing more stable localization supervision across object scales. On the AISail and RGBT-Tiny datasets, CPSF-Net achieves 92.1% and 84.2% mAP50 from unmanned surface vehicle (USV) and unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) perspectives, respectively. These results show that the proposed method performs consistently in challenging maritime environments.

title: Local-to-Global Shape-Consistent Learning for Boundary-Reliable Agricultural Object Extraction from High-Resolution Remote Sensing Imagery
summary: Accurate agricultural object extraction from high-resolution remote sensing imagery requires not only high regional segmentation accuracy but also reliable object geometry. Yet most semantic segmentation frameworks are optimized primarily for pixel- or region-level agreement, so high overlap scores can coexist with boundary discontinuities, object merging, and structurally inconsistent predictions. To address this mismatch, we propose Attention-enhanced DeepLab V3+ with Local-to-Global Shape Consistency (ADLSC), a local-to-global framework that coordinates semantic discrimination, adaptive boundary representation, and complete-object geometric consistency.
