title: Robust reinforcement learning multi-baseline phase unwrapping algorithm with JPEG-LS
summary: Multi-baseline (MB) phase unwrapping (PU) breaks through the limitations of the phase continuity assumption, but existing MBPU algorithms cannot adapt well to noisy environments. A robust reinforcement learning integer programming multi-baseline PU algorithm with JPEG-LS (RL-MBPU) is proposed. First, the cutting plane–pure integer programming cut-selection process is formulated as a sequential reinforcement-learning problem. An efficacy-guided imitation strategy is used to initialize an MBPU-structure-aware single-cut policy, which is further optimized by an actor–critic method using Cut-PAR2-based trajectory returns to reduce the root-node proof cost. Finally, the initial ambiguity number solution is corrected using dynamic median edge detector based on JPEG-LS, and the PU is completed by using the prediction of the left, top, and top-left neighbors of the current pixel and combining it with the local gradient threshold determination. In both simulation and real data experiments, the RL-MBPU algorithm demonstrated stable PU performance, including computational efficiency and noise robustness for interferograms of different sizes. Compared with the minimum-cost flow and cutting plane–pure integer programming algorithms, the RL-MBPU algorithm reduces the root mean square error by approximately 61.2% and 14.5%, respectively, while improving efficiency by approximately 54.1% and 42.4%, respectively. This can further support high-precision interferometric synthetic aperture radar applications.

title: Airborne observatory for high-resolution land surface temperature and spectral emissivity
summary: The Land surface temperature and emissivity Airborne Observatory System (LAOS) provides land surface temperature (LST) and spectral land surface emissivity (LSE) at very high spatial resolutions (0.5–4 m) and flexible (e.g., intraday) acquisition times. LAOS enables: (i) to map spectral variations in LSE—an inherent property of land surface materials—and (ii) to analyse spatial and temporal variations in LST in relation to land surface processes. Here, we present the scientific rationale for developing the system, the components of the hardware and the processing chain, and retrieval and validation results from an agricultural case study. The LAOS hardware consists of a HyperCam-LW (Telops Inc.), a Fourier transformed infrared spectrometer that operates in the long-wave infrared (7.7–11.5 µm) and an associated airborne platform. The processing chain includes radiometric calibration, generation of ortho -photo mosaics, noise removal, atmospheric correction (AC) and temperature and emissivity separation (TES). Key innovations with respect to previous airborne hyperspectral TIR studies are an improved noise filtering step and a recalibrated minimum emissivity—spectral contrast relationship derived from an extended set of ECOSTRESS spectral library spectra . For demonstrating LAOS’ capacities, an extensive survey campaign was conducted over the Burana Irrigation Consortium area near Modena, Italy, on 13–15 July 2022. Images were acquired at 1- and 4-meter resolution during three times of the day. Raw image tiles were processed to LST and LSE mosaics and compared with ground measurements. Validation was performed over agricultural surfaces – wheat stubble, melon, and water –providing a more surface-type-diverse assessment than previous more urban-focused studies. The LST mosaics show good agreement with the in-situ temperatures across all three surface types (within-class R 2 = 0.52–0.86, RMSE = 2.0–3.2 K, global R 2 = 0.96). LSE maps reveal crisp changes at field boundaries and appear relatively constant over time (i.e., both during a day and across multiple days). Airborne LSE spectra show mostly reasonable agreement with ground measurements and reproduce the overall spectral shape. Spectral emissivity remains largely stable both diurnally and across days (average variability ∼ 1.1 %), indicating consistent retrieval performance at field scale. The results demonstrate that LAOS produces LST and LSE maps with accuracies consistent with previous hyperspectral TIR studies, showcasing its potential to address pressing questions in various fields, including agriculture (e.g., irrigation), forestry (e.g., stress detection), defence (e.g., target detection), and urban studies (e.g., urban heat islands). As a high spatial resolution airborne TIR imager, LAOS can also serve as a demonstrator for upcoming satellite missions, such as LSTM (Land Surface Temperature Monitoring, ESA), TRISHNA (Thermal Infrared Satellite for High-Resolution Applications, CNES & ISRO), and Eagle-TIR (Explorer for Artemis Geology Lunar and Earth, NASA).

title: Multi-evidence-based assessment and selection of nine reconstructed solar-induced fluorescence products over China
summary: The availability of multiple long-term reconstructed solar-induced chlorophyll fluorescence (SIF) datasets at varying spatiotemporal resolutions provides new opportunities for investigating vegetation dynamics, particularly for estimating gross primary productivity (GPP) and assessing ecosystem responses to environmental stress. Evaluating the consistency and performance of reconstructed SIF (SIFr) products across different land cover types is therefore essential for their effective application in carbon–water cycle studies. In this study, we conducted a comprehensive assessment of nine widely used SIFr products (GOSIF, CSIF, RTSIF, LTSIF, HSIF, JJSIF, PKSIF, DSIF, and HCSIF) across China at a spatial resolution of 0.05° and a monthly temporal scale over the period 2007–2016. A multi-source validation framework was employed, integrating tower-based SIF, site-level and gridded GPP, and the Standardized Precipitation Evapotranspiration Index. We found that although all SIFr products exhibited strong agreement in long-term spatial patterns, substantial discrepancies existed in interannual trends. Agreement in long-term mean spatial patterns was generally higher than that in the spatial patterns of temporal trends and varied across land cover types, with stronger agreement observed in grasslands and croplands and lower agreement in forests. Across multiple validation datasets, RTSIF shows comparatively favorable performance, followed by CSIF and GOSIF, which exhibit similar performance. CSIF performs relatively well for GPP but shows lower performance in representing meteorological moisture conditions. Furthermore, product performance exhibits clear land cover dependence, with more reliable results in structurally simple ecosystems and reduced performance in complex canopy environments. We also identified differences in the relative performance of SIFr products across application scenarios and land cover types. These findings highlight the importance of product selection tailored to research objectives and environmental conditions and provide useful information for SIF-based monitoring of vegetation dynamics.

title: Enhancing soil property retrieval in an Ali-Perudic Argosols–dominated region through multi-angle hyperspectral feature integration
summary: Soil bidirectional reflectance distribution function (BRDF) is strongly influenced by soil physicochemical properties, yet most hyperspectral retrieval studies rely on single-view reflectance, leaving the value of multi-angle information insufficiently explored. In this study, bidirectional reflectance factors (BRFs) were measured at 48 viewing angles for 156 soil samples collected from a region dominated by Ali-Perudic Argosols. An optimal multi-angle retrieval framework was developed for different soil properties by systematically comparing spectral preprocessing methods, feature extraction, and modeling algorithms. The effects of viewing angle on retrieval accuracy and feature wavelength distribution were further analyzed, and the applicability of simulated multi-angle BRFs generated using SOILSPECT model was further assessed. Results show that the optimal framework for single-view reflectance combines Savitzky–Golay (SG) smoothing, a hybrid random frog–competitive adaptive reweighted sampling (RFROG–CARS) feature selection strategy, and nonlinear support vector machine (SVM) regression. Retrieval accuracy varied substantially with viewing geometry, and no universal optimal viewing angle was identified across soil properties. For multi-angle BRF data, a two-dimensional convolutional neural network (2D-CNN) feature extraction approach outperformed the RFROG–CARS wavelength selection method. Specifically, R 2 (RMSE) improved from 0.64 (8.8 g/kg) to 0.73 (7.7 g/kg) for SOM content, from 0.53 (6.9 %) to 0.61 (6.3 %) for sand content, and from 0.64 (4.7 %) to 0.69 (4.4 %) for silt content, while remaining comparable for cation exchange capacity (0.77/2.4 cmol/kg to 0.76/2.4 cmol/kg) and clay content (0.80/4.3 % to 0.79/4.3 %). Although the retrieval accuracy based on multi-angle BRFs remained slightly lower than that obtained from the optimal viewing geometry, it consistently outperformed most individual viewing angles. The selected multi-angle hyperspectral features were distributed across nearly all viewing angles, indicating complementary spectral–geometric information. Although retrieval accuracy based on simulated BRFs was lower than that based on measured BRFs, the results were broadly comparable. These findings support the use of multi-angle information in soil spectroscopy and remote sensing applications.

title: PRINT: A semi-empirical canopy water removal approach for improving estimates of leaf nitrogen and grain protein contents in winter wheat
summary: Accurate estimation of leaf nitrogen content (LNC) and grain protein content (GPC) in winter wheat is crucial for making fertilization recommendations and assessing grain quality. Previous methods primarily relied on chlorophyll (Chl)-sensitive vegetation indices from the visible and near-infrared domain, while shortwave-infrared spectral features linked to dry matter and nitrogen remain underutilized due to strong leaf water masking. Although existing water removal methods can mitigate the absorption effects of leaf water, the reliability of the resulting simulated dry-canopy reflectance spectra (SDR) is limited by inaccurate leaf mass per area (LMA) retrieval. This study aimed to develop a semi-empirical water removal approach by integrating PRior knowledge and INitialization of leaf water conTent and LMA (PRINT) to simulate SDR, with the objective of improving the estimation performance of LNC and GPC. To achieve this goal, a Random Forest-based hybrid retrieval model was developed to increase LMA retrieval accuracy. Meanwhile, a visible and shortwave-based nitrogen index (VSNI) by combining the visible (proxy of Chl) and shortwave-infrared features was proposed for improving estimation performance of LNC and GPC. Moreover, experimental datasets covering multiple growth stages and geographic sites were collected to improve sample representativeness. These datasets were utilized to improve the retrieval of LMA and evaluate the performance of LNC and GPC estimations. The results demonstrated that the PRINT significantly improved the estimation accuracy of LMA over two standard physically-based inversion models (RMSE: 6.23 g/m 2 vs 8.25 g/m 2 and 45.73 g/m 2 ). Compared with existing VI-based models, the VSNI-based models yielded substantial improvements in LNC (R 2 : 0.62 ∼ 0.65, RMSE = 0.42 ∼ 0.54%) across sites, and enhanced GPC estimation accuracy up to R 2 = 0.66 (RMSE = 0.70%) at the peak filling stage across two years at one site. The proposed methodology advances the spectroscopic understanding of shortwave-infrared responses to nitrogen-related agronomic biochemicals, and holds significant potential for future applications in large-scale growth monitoring of wheat systems using satellite imagery.

title: High-resolution mapping of urban wet-bulb temperature and its intra-urban variability: A London case study
summary: Most extreme-heat studies map high-resolution near-surface dry-bulb air temperature ( T a ), yet wet-bulb temperature ( T w ) fields that can capture the combined effects of T a and humidity to represent human heat stress remain limited. This data gap constrains investigation of intra-urban heat variability and the timing of peak heat stress. Here, based on the Rankine-Kirchhoff approximations of Romps, this study innovatively generates hourly 1-km T w by integrating crowdsourced station observations with remote sensing and reanalysis data in machine learning based downscaling frameworks. Taking London during the summers of 2019–2022 as a case study, the tuned RF-based downscaling approach achieved the best performance ( MAE = 0.65 °C, RMSE = 0.93 °C, R 2 = 0.91) among all models. The resulting T w patterns diverge from those commonly reported for T a : blue infrastructure shows no consistent cooling effect, whereas vegetated areas cool T w increasingly as tree cover rises, pointing to tree-dominated green infrastructure as a promising humid-heat countermeasure. Results further show that daily maximum T w occurs 0.7 h earlier than daily maximum T a in London, opposite to findings elsewhere, implying that climate type and coastal influence modulate the timing of peak T w , which may affect the attribution of excess nighttime mortality. Besides, a systematic global assessment of the mechanisms controlling T w extremes is also required in the future.

title: Remote sensing of lake surface water temperature reveals divergent hydroclimatic associations with lake ice phenology across China
summary: Lake ice phenology is a sensitive indicator of climate change, yet its regional hydroclimatic associations remain poorly understood. Here, we reconstructed daily lake surface water temperature (LSWT) from MODIS for 583 lakes across China and derived freeze-up date (FUD), break-up date (BUD), and ice cover duration (ICD) for 376 seasonally ice-covered lakes. Robustness was evaluated with sensitivity tests, meteorological observations, transition-period comparisons, and passive-microwave ice records; Mann-Kendall tests, Theil-Sen slopes, VIF-constrained XGBoost-SHAP, and structural equation modeling assessed trends and regional associations. FUD was delayed in all three ice-covered regions, whereas BUD was delayed in the Tibetan Plateau Lake Region (TPR) but advanced in the Mongolian-Xinjiang Lake Region (MXR) and Northeast Lake Region (NLR), resulting in shorter ICD in all regions. Regional mean ICD declined by 0.03, 0.35, and 0.47 d yr -1 in the TPR, MXR, and NLR, respectively; significant lake-level changes were concentrated in the TPR, with 72 and 33 lakes showing significant FUD and BUD trends. All nine models retained positive hold-out R 2 (0.535–0.960). SHAP attributions differed by region: radiative variables dominated in the TPR, the MXR showed metric-specific associations with wind, snowfall, geographic, and thermal , and geographic, radiative, and morphometric variables dominated in the NLR. Structural equation models indicated stronger precipitation-related associations in the NLR and snowfall-related associations in the MXR and TPR. These results reveal pronounced regional heterogeneity in lake ice responses to warming and the value of integrating remote sensing, interpretable machine learning, and pathway modeling to resolve these contrasts.

title: Quantitative analysis of small-scale roughness effects in spaceborne GNSS reflectometry informed by L-band microwave radiometry
summary: Spaceborne Global Navigation Satellite System Reflectometry (GNSS-R) has shown great potential for terrestrial monitoring, but the compensation of small-scale surface roughness remains an important challenge. In particular, the root-mean-square surface height σ h , its incidence angle dependence represented by n in c o s n θ , and their relationships with soil moisture (SM) are still insufficiently characterized for spaceborne GNSS-R. In this study, CYGNSS surface reflectivity (SR) observations are combined with model-simulated smooth bare-soil reflectivity derived from SMOS SM and vegetation attenuation represented by SMOS-IC L-band Vegetation Optical Depth (L-VOD). Global σ h and n are estimated on a 25 km grid by fitting the model predictions to CYGNSS observations. The retrieved σ h is compared to multiple topographic variables, SMAP and SMOS-IC roughness parameters, and Saharan aerodynamic roughness measurements, while the dependence of n on vegetation and land cover is also investigated. Results show that the retrieved σ h is more strongly associated with terrain descriptors such as uniformity, Shannon index, entropy, Northness, and Eastness than with conventional elevation- and slope-based variables. Both σ h and n also exhibit relationships with SM and vegetation, indicating potential coupling between effective roughness characterization and vegetation-related uncertainties. After compensation for vegetation and roughness effects, CYGNSS SR shows good consistency with simulated bare soil SR. Additional evaluation using in situ SM observations from the International Soil Moisture Network further supports the effectiveness of the retrieved parameters. Overall, these findings offer valuable insights into the use of physics-based empirical or semi-empirical models in spaceborne GNSS-R for soil moisture retrievals and other terrestrial applications.

title: 3D building wireframe reconstruction via edge point regression
summary: Despite significant progress in point cloud–based 3D building reconstruction, the effectiveness of existing methods remains constrained by four major bottlenecks. These include the scarcity of high-quality annotated datasets, the pervasive incompleteness and noise in real-world point clouds, the substantial memory consumption incurred by the edge search space, and the lack of adequate geometric constraints in network designs, which often causes loss functions to fail in capturing the underlying 3D structural regularities. To address these challenges, we pre-train a self-supervised learning (SSL) framework on large-scale unlabeled point clouds to learn generic geometric representations, and subsequently fine-tune it using only a limited set of annotated roof samples for 3D wireframe reconstruction. The key contribution of this work is the proposal of a new SSL-based framework that utilizes geometry aware edge point identification to facilitate wireframe reconstruction and avoid missing corners, thereby mitigating issues related to dataset quality and computational complexity. Specifically, the framework first leverages a pretrained SSL-based feature extractor to generate robust point-wise representations under sparse and imperfect inputs. Building on these features, an edge point–guided regression module predicts the parametric attributes of roof wireframes. To effectively supervise the training of this regression module, we formulate a joint loss function that optimizes two complementary objectives: (1) minimizing the Euclidean distance between input points and their nearest line segments, and (2) reducing the distance between candidate edge points and their projections on the reconstructed model. Coupled with bipartite edge matching and an edge-aware non-maximum suppression strategy, the proposed method ensures geometric validity while reducing computational redundancy. Extensive experiments across three datasets of varying geometric complexity and scale (Dense, Building3D, and the large-scale Tallinn City dataset) demonstrate the framework’s effectiveness. The SSL-based pretrained model attains 97% corner precision and 91% edge precision for wireframe reconstruction on the Building3D dataset, surpassing conventional baselines and approaching the performance of fully supervised methods. Remarkably, even under limited supervision, specifically utilizing only 50% partially labeled data during fine-tuning, the model maintains strong accuracy with 86% corner precision and 67% edge precision, underscoring its advantages over current SSL-based approaches.

title: MMC-Net: Mamba-based multi-level class-aware network for panchromatic and multispectral fusion classification
summary: Recent advances in remote sensing (RS) have improved panchromatic (PAN) and multispectral (MS) data acquisition, but challenges remain in multi-source fusion classification due to limitations in non-redundant feature extraction (i.e., effectively preserving complementary information while suppressing source-specific redundancies) and cross-source alignment (i.e., accurately matching spatial–spectral correspondences between PAN and MS data). The emerging state space model (SSM)-based Mamba model, with its global modeling and linear complexity, shows potential for complex land cover classification tasks. To this end, we propose MMC-Net, a novel Mamba-based multi-level class-aware network for PAN and MS fusion classification, which integrates a progressive fusion feature learning (PFFL) module and a multi-branch class-aware classification (MBCAC) module. The PFFL module employs dual-path spatial–spectral Mamba (S 2 Mamba) to extract discriminative features while suppressing redundancy through the feature reconstruction module (FRM), along with fusion Mamba (FMamba) to enable cross-source interaction via channel exchange and Fusion SSM. The MBCAC module enhances classification diversity through spatial-wise softmax and multi-branch learning, while its parameter-sharing mechanism across levels captures hierarchical discriminative patterns. Validated on three PAN-MS and one HSI-LiDAR datasets, MMC-Net achieves state-of-the-art performance and demonstrates robust, source-agnostic generalization across heterogeneous modalities. The code is available at https://github.com/Xidian-AIGroup190726/MMCNet .

title: Global offshore wind development (2015–2025): multiscale structural evolution based on object-level sar mapping
summary: Offshore wind is an important renewable infrastructure supporting the global energy transition, making accurate offshore wind turbine (OWT) mapping essential for understanding infrastructure expansion and informing marine spatial management. Existing long-term approaches often extend single-period detections over time based on structural-stability assumptions, but accumulated identification errors and regional imaging differences limit consistent object-level representation across years and regions. To address this challenge, this study proposes a coordinated three-stage object-level SAR mapping framework, in which a stable and balanced sample representation strategy under unified annual temporal windows provides a consistent data basis across regions and years. On this basis, the lightweight YOLO-SAR model integrates frequency-aware feature modeling and hierarchical structural representation to improve OWT detection under heterogeneous conditions. Compared with YOLO11n, YOLO-SAR reduces the parameter count from 2.58 M to 2.30 M while improving mAP@0.5:0.95 from 0.3956 to 0.4553. Spatial reconstruction then transforms detection outputs into consistent annual object-level OWT maps, forming a continuous spatial database covering 2015–2025. Multi-region validation and comparisons with public datasets further support the reliability of these spatial records. These records reveal multiscale patterns of offshore wind spatial evolution: shifts in regional contributions reshape global growth, regional expansion pathways and internal spatial restructuring exhibit stage-dependent differences, and site-boundary expansion and turbine-spacing adjustments determine local spatial organization. These findings demonstrate that global offshore wind development is not merely a process of quantitative growth, but a multiscale spatial evolution driven by regional shifts, site expansion, and internal spatial reorganization. The proposed framework provides a consistent data foundation for global offshore wind evolution analysis and can be extended to other marine energy infrastructures.

title: A physics-constrained superpixel-based multi-source remote sensing spatiotemporal fusion network
summary: Remote sensing spatiotemporal fusion aims to generate image sequences with both high spatial and temporal resolution. However, many deep learning approaches treat fusion as a black-box regression problem, overlooking differences in sensor imaging physics—such as the point spread function (PSF) and pixel-area integration—which often leads to boundary blurring, spectral mixing, or even physically implausible high-frequency details over heterogeneous landscapes. In addition, these methods commonly rely on paired coarse-/fine-resolution reference images at the same time, which limits data availability. To address these issues, we propose SPP-STF, a superpixel-based fusion network trained with a physics-guided degradation-consistency regularizer that requires only a reference fine-resolution image and a target coarse-resolution observation, while deriving an edge intensity map as a structural prior. The model adopts a U-Net-style, three-branch encoder–decoder to fuse texture, temporal variation, and edge cues at multiple scales. An EdgeResBlock uses high-frequency gating to sharpen boundaries and reduce cross-class leakage, and a superpixel cross-attention Transformer learns object-level correspondences to alleviate alignment errors caused by mixed pixels. During training, we introduce a learnable anisotropic Gaussian PSF-based degradation-consistency term: the predicted fine-resolution output is blurred and downsampled via area integration to match the observed coarse image, and this term is optimized jointly with the reconstruction loss. Quantitatively, SPP-STF achieves the best RMSE, SAM, PSNR, and UIQI on CIA (0.0254, 0.1522, 31.9330 dB, and 0.8451), the best results across all six metrics on LGC (including RMSE 0.0188 and PSNR 34.6307 dB), and the best RMSE, SSIM, SAM, PSNR, and ERGAS on Tianjin (0.0410, 0.7640, 0.2459, 27.8666 dB, and 30.4838). Ablation studies confirm the complementary benefits of the superpixel and edge modules. The PSF term is interpreted here as a training-time regularizer that provides consistent and physically more reasonable improvements across the three datasets. Structured pruning further indicates that the model can retain spatial structure under substantial compression, while spectral fidelity becomes notably more sensitive beyond roughly 70% pruning.
